## Natural history notes

A medium-sized gilled mushroom characterized by a tan to golden-brown cap, dark purplish-brown spores, and a tendency for the flesh to bruise bluish when handled or damaged. In Florida, it is most often associated with warm, humid open habitats such as pastures, grassy fields, and livestock areas, where it grows from dung-enriched soils. This species is psychoactive and should not be consumed; mushroom identification can be difficult and potentially dangerous, and possession or use may be legally restricted depending on location.
